players.product: Gemma Power Systems EPC for combined-cycle gas plants serving data-center load (4.1 GW in backlog) plus data-center thermal expansion / energy storage tank fabrication

quarterly_data.signal: Fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 (ended January 31, 2026) results as given by the CEO and CFO: record revenue of $262.1 million in Q4 (up 13%, driven by timing of Power segment projects as Trumbull reached substantial completion and recently awarded projects ramped) and record revenue of $944.6 million for fiscal 2026 (up 8.1%); Q4 gross margin 25% and full-year gross margin 20.5% (vs 16.1% in fiscal 2025); record Q4 net income $49.2 million ($3.47 per diluted share) and fiscal 2026 net income $137.8 million; Q4 EBITDA $56 million (21.4% margin) and fiscal 2026 EBITDA $162.8 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $262.1 million (+13%); FY2026 revenue $944.6 million (+8.1%); Q4 gross margin 25%; Q4 net income $49.2 million; Q4 EBITDA $56 million

quarterly_data.signal: Backlog and awards: during fiscal 2026 Argan added $2.5 billion in new contract value, lifting consolidated project backlog to $2.9 billion at January 31, 2026, including three gas-fired power plants in the United States totaling over 3.4 gigawatts; backlog is approximately 77% natural gas projects, 14% renewable and 9% industrial, and the CEO expects natural gas to remain a substantial portion of backlog for the near and midterm. The $2.9 billion backlog is fully committed and will be translated into revenues over the next 3-plus years.
quarterly_data.figure: $2.5 billion new contract value; backlog $2.9 billion; three gas plants totaling over 3.4 gigawatts; mix 77% gas / 14% renewable / 9% industrial

quarterly_data.signal: Demand drivers named by the CEO: 'rapid growth in AI and data centers, electrification of everything, the need to replace aging power facilities and years of underinvestment in power infrastructure are driving urgent demand for new, reliable power generation capacity'; aging thermal infrastructure could constrain the 24/7 energy needed to run data centers, and 'Only a handful of companies, including Argan, are capable of building the large, complex combined-cycle facilities'.

Segment detail for Q4 FY2026: Power segment revenues $204 million (vs $197 million a year earlier), 78% of consolidated revenues, pretax book income $55 million; Industrial segment revenue $53 million (vs $33 million), 20% of revenues, pretax book income approximately $4 million; Teledata revenue $5 million with backlog of $8.4 million (Teledata also works with data centers). Segment gross margins were 29% (Power), 11% (Industrial) and 14.2% (Teledata); the CEO attributed the 29% Power margin to execution, a slight rotation toward a gas-heavy backlog, and early substantial completion at Trumbull avoiding certain costs.
quarterly_data.figure: Power $204 million (78%), pretax $55 million, gross margin 29%; Industrial $53 million (20%); Teledata $5 million, backlog $8.4 million

quarterly_data.signal: Project status: substantial completion in December 2025, ahead of schedule, on the 950-megawatt Trumbull Energy Center; continued progress on the 1.2 gigawatt ultra-efficient combined-cycle natural gas plant for SLEC in Texas; early work begun on two more Texas gas projects, the 1.4 gigawatt project with CPV and an 860-megawatt project; the 700-megawatt combined-cycle gas plant in the U.S. progressing well; in Ireland, the 300-megawatt Tarbert biofuel plant for SSE Thermal and a 170-megawatt thermal facility continue to progress.
quarterly_data.figure: 950-megawatt Trumbull substantial completion; 1.2 gigawatt SLEC; 1.4 gigawatt CPV; 860-megawatt; 700-megawatt; 300-megawatt Tarbert; 170-megawatt Ireland

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline and capacity (point-in-time guidance): CEO expects to add 'a handful of new projects over the next 12 to 20 months' (in Q&A: 'over the next 8 to 20 months'); capacity is 10 to 12 jobs simultaneously, with 9 underway (7 thermal and 2 renewable) and Trumbull at the tail end, so Argan has capacity to take on additional jobs this year. Behind-the-meter projects remain a robust opportunity evaluated case by case; the PJM emergency capacity procurement auction could have the same pull-forward effect as the Texas Energy Fund.
quarterly_data.figure: handful of new projects over the next 12 to 20 months; capacity 10 to 12 jobs; 9 underway, 7 thermal and 2 renewable

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center work in the Industrial segment (Roberts): a data center project valued at $125 million was added during the year; Industrial revenue rose from $29 million in Q1 to $53 million in Q4, and the CEO looks forward to increased year-over-year growth for this business.
quarterly_data.figure: $125 million data center project; Industrial revenue $29 million (Q1) to $53 million (Q4)

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain and labor: the CEO said that from a supply chain, turbine and interconnection standpoint 'there's a fair amount of improving conditions there as the supply chain tries to catch up and meet up with the increased demand, not just in the United States, but globally'; 'the constraints, it's people at all levels' (project leadership, craft and back office), and the non-craft workforce is at the highest level it has ever been.

Pricing and margin outlook: the CEO said 'there's enough work for everyone, and our pricing model remains the same as it always has', pricing for market, inflation, labor and risk; the CFO said quarterly margins over the last 2 years ranged between 11.4% to 25% and 'It's a little too early to tell where fiscal year '27 will end up from a gross margin standpoint'.
quarterly_data.figure: quarterly margins between 11.4% to 25% over the last 2 years; no FY2027 margin guidance

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and capital return at January 31, 2026: approximately $895 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments, net liquidity $421 million (up $120 million from $301 million) and no debt; stockholders' equity $462 million; $43 million returned to shareholders in fiscal 2026; quarterly dividend raised 33% to $0.50 in September 2025; buyback authorization increased to $150 million in April 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: $895 million cash and investments; net liquidity $421 million; no debt; $43 million returned in fiscal 2026
